builder_plan.scenario: Start with one repeated product task that has a measurable failure or cost.
builder_plan.change: Read the methods and identify one change you can isolate in that workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current implementation on the same held-out tasks.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful outcomes, response time, human rework, and total cost per successful task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Toward Open ISA Supercomputing: A Comparative Study of RISC-V, Arm, and x86 Architectures on HPC Workloads
summary: This is a comparative hardware evaluation, not a technique: it benchmarks Sophgo SG2044 (RISC-V), NVIDIA Grace, and Intel Xeon 8480+ on HPC kernels and llama.cpp under a common software stack, replacing anecdotal cross-platform comparisons with a uniform methodology. Adoption would mean procuring RISC-V server hardware, which costs capital budget, toolchain maturity, and 8-15x lower absolute FP64 and memory-bandwidth performance versus incumbent x86 or Arm nodes. The finding can fail to transfer because llama.cpp decode efficiency on SG2044 depends on L2-aware process placement, saturates beyond memory bandwidth limits, and reflects a specific quantization and workload configuration.
rationale: The paper's only ML-relevant result is efficient LLM decode on RISC-V hardware the reader does not own and cannot access via their existing GPU or API constraints, so it is worth monitoring as a future low-cost inference platform rather than adopting now.
technique: RISC-V vs Arm vs x86 HPC benchmark comparison

claims.statement: This is a comparative hardware evaluation, not a technique: it benchmarks Sophgo SG2044 (RISC-V), NVIDIA Grace, and Intel Xeon 8480+ on HPC kernels and llama.cpp under a common software stack, replacing anecdotal cross-platform comparisons with a uniform methodology. Adoption would mean procuring RISC-V server hardware, which costs capital budget, toolchain maturity, and 8-15x lower absolute FP64 and memory-bandwidth performance versus incumbent x86 or Arm nodes. The finding can fail to transfer because llama.cpp decode efficiency on SG2044 depends on L2-aware process placement, saturates beyond memory bandwidth limits, and reflects a specific quantization and workload configuration.

The 64-core RISC-V SG2044 delivers the highest relative scaling and energy efficiency on LLM decode among the evaluated platforms and exceeds the Intel Xeon Platinum 8480+ in decode throughput, while showing 8-15x less absolute performance than the Arm and x86 systems overall.
